core.title: Make every exposed journey reachable from the composition root through the journey runner
core.given: a journey document (a plan artifact, layout.plan_item) declares entrypoint.exposed=true and a composition root exists (roles.composition_root)
core.when: the repository is in that state (standing invariant; pre-existing violations count, edits are not required)
core.then: every declared entrypoint action of that journey MUST be reachable from the composition root via a route-table entry (idiom.action_route_map) that binds the action to that same journey document, by its journey identifier and its canonical journey document path (layout.plan_item).
prefer: Dispatch journey routes through the journey runner (idiom.journey_runner) — the composition root MUST reference it — so dispatch runs composition root -> journey runner -> the runners below it.
Keep journey routes additive to the existing route forms in the route table: the direct train route (urn.train) and the grouping route.
avoid: Restating continuation edges in the route table; it only establishes external reachability, and the journey document is authoritative for continuation topology.
Weakening existing direct-train or grouping mappings.
Binding a route entry to a journey identifier or document other than the declaring one, or bypassing the journey runner.
unless: entrypoint.exposed=false: internal journeys are intentionally not reachable from the composition root.
No composition root exists yet (planning phase), as for exposed grouping artifacts.
core.why: An exposed journey is executable only if the public entry reaches it through the journey runner (idiom.journey_runner); this closes the public entry direction of the journey topology.
evidence: The check reads the journey documents (layout.plan_item), selects exposed ones, and reports no unmapped action: each declared action is bound to the same journey identifier and document path in the composition root's route table.
The composition root references the journey runner (idiom.journey_runner).
Journey route values do not restate continuation edges, and existing direct-train and grouping mappings are not weakened.
verification: Scope: the check scans the journey document tree (layout.plan_item), selects documents whose entrypoint is declared exposed, and skips documents declared internal.

For each declared entrypoint action of an exposed journey, the check requires a route-table entry (idiom.action_route_map) in the composition root whose value binds the declaring document's journey identifier and its canonical journey document path (layout.plan_item).
The check requires the composition root to reference the journey runner (idiom.journey_runner) whenever an exposed journey exists, independent of whether any journey entries exist in the route table.
The route table admits three additive route forms (direct train, grouping, journey; idiom.action_route_map, urn.train); only the journey form is covered by this check.
The check emits no finding when the repository has no composition root yet (planning phase).
Severity 4; disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding.

Standing invariant: the check inspects whole-repository state, not only the current change; pre-existing violations are findings, and the change facts are discovery hints only, not enforcement prerequisites.
Term journey_reachability: the declaration-to-composition-root binding that makes an exposed journey executable.
Term journey_mapping: a composition-root route-table value binding a journey identifier and the canonical journey document path.

values: journey document (plan artifact declaring an entrypoint)
journey document entrypoint exposure or entrypoint actions edited
composition-root journey route entries or journey-runner reference edited
exposed journey action unmapped or mis-mapped in the composition root's route table
composition root does not reference the journey runner while an exposed journey exists

fires: An exposed journey (entrypoint.exposed=true) has a declared entrypoint action with no route-table entry in the composition root, whether or not the current task edited it.
A route-table entry for an exposed journey action binds a different journey identifier or document path than the declaring journey document.
An exposed journey exists and the composition root does not reference the journey runner, even if the route table has no journey entries yet.
A change touches only direct-train or grouping mappings while an exposed journey action is already unmapped.
doesNotFire: The journey document declares entrypoint.exposed=false (internal journey).
The repository is in the planning phase and has no composition root yet.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the composition root lives; its presence is the condition under which the reachability obligation applies.
The stack's local name for the composition root, used throughout the Bun texts.
Where journey documents (plan artifacts declaring an entrypoint) live, and the canonical path a journey route entry must point to; the check's discovery scope is derived from this pattern.
profileRequirements.bunValue: plan/_journeys/<id>.yaml; journey documents discovered at plan/_journeys/**/*.yaml

profileRequirements.meaning: The composition-root construct that maps each entrypoint action to a route, with its additive route forms; the journey form binds { journeyId, path }.
profileRequirements.bunValue: JOURNEY_MAP in server.ts; additive forms: "train:<subject>:<slug>", { interlockingId, path }, { journeyId, path }

profileRequirements.meaning: The construct through which the composition root dispatches a journey route, and which it must reference.
profileRequirements.bunValue: JourneyRunner; Station Master -> JourneyRunner(journeyPath) -> InterlockingRunner -> TrainRunner

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape of the direct train route form that journey routes must stay additive to.

proposedKeys.meaning: The composition-root construct that maps each entrypoint action to a route (direct train, grouping, or journey form).
proposedKeys.bunValue: JOURNEY_MAP in server.ts; additive forms: "train:<subject>:<slug>", { interlockingId, path }, { journeyId, path }
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.route_handler describes a boundary handler, not the composition root's action-to-route table; no existing key names the route table or its entry forms.

proposedKeys.meaning: The construct through which the composition root dispatches a journey route, and which the composition root must reference.
proposedKeys.bunValue: JourneyRunner; Station Master -> JourneyRunner(journeyPath) -> InterlockingRunner -> TrainRunner
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.machinery covers delivery machinery (server, transport, runtime), not the domain dispatch runner for journeys; no existing key names the journey runner.

bunOnly.reason: Language/runtime scoping is realization-only; the neutral core activates on artifact roles and plan artifacts, never on a language or runtime.
The validator/finding id of this one rule is a realization detail; the core's verification names the check generically and the core finding fact uses a role-level description.

neutralityNotes: The journey document's own schema (entrypoint.exposed, journey_id, declared entrypoint actions) is treated as stack-neutral plan-artifact data, not stack mechanism, so those field names appear in the core verbatim; if another stack's journey documents declare exposure differently, a profile key for the exposure declaration would be needed. The journey document's location and canonical path are carried by layout.plan_item (a journey document is a plan artifact), whose Bun value is the journey tree plan/_journeys/<id>.yaml with discovery scope plan/_journeys/**/*.yaml. The stack names Station Master, server.ts, JOURNEY_MAP and JourneyRunner are realized through profile keys (roles.composition_root.name/path and the proposed idiom.action_route_map / idiom.journey_runner). "Interlocking" has no vocabulary key, so the core says "grouping"; the concrete grouping route form { interlockingId, path } and the runner chain JourneyRunner -> InterlockingRunner -> TrainRunner are carried inside idiom.action_route_map and idiom.journey_runner bunValues. Severity and disposition stay in core verification; the validator and finding ids are bunOnly.
